title: Ukrainian man sets himself on fire in Warsaw protesting equal treatment

tea.why: A Ukrainian man carried out a self-immolation act in Warsaw to demand equal treatment for Ukrainian citizens compared to Polish citizens.
tea.want: Equal treatment for Ukrainian citizens in Poland compared to Poles.
tea.changed: Nov 26: Hospital officials confirmed the man is alive in the intensive care unit with critical burns.

summary: On the evening of November 25, a 22-year-old Ukrainian citizen set himself on fire in central Warsaw on the square between the Presidential Palace and the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage building. According to media reports citing outlets like Fakt, the individual was protesting discrimination and demanding that Ukrainian citizens be treated on equal terms with Poles. Passersby intervened with a fire extinguisher before Government Protection Service officers called emergency services. The man sustained severe, critical burns to his face, back, arms, legs, and upper respiratory tract, and was transported to the Military Institute of Medicine in Warsaw. Authorities and investigators are examining potential motives, including a political protest regarding the treatment of Ukrainians and personal or academic challenges.
demands: Equal treatment for Ukrainian citizens in Poland
response: According to reports, Government Protection Service officers on duty called the fire department and an ambulance. Poland's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Administration confirmed the victim's identity, while investigators are examining potential political and personal motives.

updates.text: A 22-year-old Ukrainian man set himself on fire outside the Presidential Palace in Warsaw, sustaining severe burns.
The Military Institute of Medicine hospital confirmed that the man is alive and receiving treatment in intensive care.

sources.title: Man who set himself on fire in Warsaw demanded equal treatment for Ukrainian citizens
